mechanism: lidar_buffer is a deque(maxlen=lidar_seq_len*data_save_freq=1*5=5) appended with the current full cloud every run_step. HEAD reads [-(i+1)] = [-1] = newest; the pre-fix code reads [i] = [0] = oldest = 4 ticks old (200 ms at 20 FPS sync, action_repeat=1). With lidar_seq_len=1 the realign branch is skipped, so the stale cloud is fed to the network in the ego frame of 4 ticks ago (commit message: "LiDAR was 100ms delayed due to accessing a queue from the wrong side"). Active in our host for ANY lidar spec, because the buffer fills once per tick regardless of sweep fraction.
expected_pre_behaviour: Perception of moving actors lags by ~0.2 s: braking/evasion starts later for cut-ins, crossers and oncoming drifters; static/slow leads shift by ego displacement only (v*0.2 s, <=1.6 m at 8 m/s) so LeadStopped is near-inert.

mechanism: With SLOWER=1 (default) the target-speed classes 2 and 3 are lowered before inference. HEAD: [0,2,5,8] -> [0,2,3,6] m/s; reverted: [0,2,4,7] m/s. The expected target speed = sum(softmax * target_speeds) (uncertainty weighting) feeds the longitudinal PID, so the reverted version drives ~1 m/s faster in every non-brake state and brakes from a higher speed. The route_scenario_local.py part of cf59098 is leaderboard-side and not in team_code; it is NOT reverted.
expected_pre_behaviour: Higher cruise speed (~7 vs ~6 m/s) and longer stopping distance in every scenario; more/earlier contacts where the margin is tight (CutIn, LeadDecel, CrossingTraffic); the 2023 camera-ready note calls the 2 m/s offset a bugfix for longest6 (overconfident classifier brakes late).
